scope: Delete the denial-opener ids from a quantized artifact: the tokenizer arrays, the scalar ids that share the vocabulary id space, and the token-row matrix. Storage fidelity, the renumbering map, and the static encoder paths of the deleted surfaces. No model is loaded and no behavioural claim is made.
method: The denial surfaces of the opener table are resolved against the artifact tokenizer in both contexts (bare and with the leading space); every id a surface resolves to in a single token is a deletion candidate. A candidate is deleted when its stored token_type is NORMAL and, unless the byte-alphabet arm is asked for, its piece is more than one raw byte (a single raw byte IS the tokenizer's alphabet). The write rebuilds the GGUF container: tokenizer.ggml.tokens and tokenizer.ggml.token_type lose the entries, every scalar *_token_id is renumbered down by the number of deleted ids below it, and each vocabulary-wide token-row matrix loses the rows (surviving rows are copied as whole stored rows). Every other KV entry and tensor payload is copied verbatim; tensor offsets are recomputed under the file alignment. The revert sidecar stores the deleted entries and raw row bytes and re-inserts them. No model is loaded and no logits are read; the encoder paths are string automata over the metadata: llama.cpp's byte-level BPE plus its byte fallback (whose behaviour for the deleted symbols was checked against llama-tokenize on the written file) and the reference byte-alphabet fallback.
gated: Whether the model then refuses less is out of scope: that needs a serve/forward pass, which this card forbids. Even the static result is limited — a merged token whose bytes survive is still spellable as a sequence, so the model can emit the denial string in several tokens; the deleted id is gone, the string is not.

discovery.how: vocabulary-wide 2-D tensors are found by row count == tokenizer vocabulary; the artifact name decides the role

policy.definition: candidates are the ids the table's denial surfaces resolve to in one token in either context; a candidate is deleted when its token_type is NORMAL and, unless --include-byte-alphabet, its piece is more than one raw byte

renumber.rule: new_id = old_id - (number of deleted ids below old_id)
renumber.invariant: every surviving id keeps its piece and its row: the token at new_id is the token that was at old_id, and no surviving piece changes

encode.algorithm: byte-level BPE merge ranks (tokenizer.ggml.merges), then the vocabulary lookup; a merged symbol absent from the vocabulary falls back byte by byte. ``after`` models llama.cpp exactly (src/llama-vocab.cpp: each UTF-8 byte of the unknown symbol is looked up as a token text, so a non-ASCII byte is DROPPED); ``after_reference`` models the byte-alphabet fallback Hugging Face uses (the symbol is mapped back through the byte alphabet and every byte is looked up). Tokenization only; the llama.cpp path was checked against llama-tokenize on the written artifact.
encode.divergence: llama.cpp rebuilds a deleted merged symbol from the merge list and then loses every non-ASCII byte of it: the leading-space marker Ġ is two UTF-8 bytes with no single-byte token text, so it is dropped and " Sorry" encodes as the five byte tokens of "Sorry". The reference path keeps the space as token 220. Both paths leave the string spellable; neither can produce the deleted id.

tensors.name: token_embd.weight
tensors.row_policy: whole stored rows are copied for surviving rows and the deleted rows are dropped; no value is re-encoded, so every surviving row is byte-identical

arrays_touched.untouched: tokenizer.ggml.merges and every other KV entry keep their exact encoding; every other tensor keeps its payload; only offsets after the shrunken matrix move
arrays_touched.renumbering_ties: the tokenizer arrays, the scalar id fields and the matrix rows share one id space. A file that renumbers one without the others is broken: a token id that disagrees with its row reads the wrong embedding, and a scalar id that is not renumbered points at a different token. This is why the report names every one of them.

plan.writer: jdewitt.vocabdelete._write_container: KV entries verbatim except the named ones, tensor payloads streamed from the source except the shrunken matrices, offsets recomputed under the file alignment

notes: deletion removes a single-token id; a merged token whose bytes survive is still spellable as a sequence, so this edit does not make the string unsampleable

llama.cpp rebuilds the deleted merged symbol and then drops every non-ASCII byte of it: the leading-space marker (Ġ) is lost on encode, so " Sorry" becomes the five byte tokens of "Sorry". The space token itself survives, so generation can still emit it
a byte-alphabet id cannot be deleted without breaking every string that uses its byte
removal_measured is false: no forward pass, no logits, no serve

metadata.note: every KV entry not in changed_entries is byte-identical, including tokenizer.ggml.merges and the chat template

reencode.note: computed from the written file's tokenizer.ggml arrays, not from the plan; encode models llama.cpp's byte fallback (verified against llama-tokenize), encode_reference the byte-alphabet fallback

revert.note: the source is reconstructed from the sidecar (deleted entries and raw row bytes re-inserted), not copied; byte_exact compares the digest with the recorded source
